one_liner: SaaS platform for building, hosting, and running online stores and their backend commerce operations.
self_serve_evidence: Merchants can self-serve generate custom-app access tokens directly in the Shopify Admin with no review, but public apps distributed via the Shopify App Store go through Shopify's partner review process.
api_surface: GraphQL Admin API (primary, very broad: products, orders, customers, inventory, fulfillment, checkout) plus a legacy REST Admin API and a separate Storefront API; extremely mature and well-documented.
existing_mcp_detail: Shopify/dev-mcp (official shopify.dev MCP server) and an official Storefront MCP for agentic shopping.
notes: One of the most agent-ready ecommerce APIs; Shopify is actively investing in first-party MCP tooling.

one_liner: Open-source e-commerce plugin that turns a WordPress site into an online store.
self_serve_evidence: Store owners generate REST API consumer key/secret pairs themselves under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API with no approval process.
api_surface: REST API (v1-v3) covering products, orders, customers, coupons, reports, and webhooks; since it's self-hosted, exact surface/version depends on each store's install and plugin version.
notes: No central multi-tenant auth (each self-hosted store issues its own keys), but per-store integration is trivial and self-serve.

one_liner: SaaS e-commerce platform for building hosted or headless online stores.
self_serve_evidence: Merchants generate store-level API accounts directly in the control panel, and developers register apps via the Developer Portal without a hard approval gate to start building.
api_surface: REST (V2/V3 Admin) plus GraphQL (Storefront, Admin, and Account APIs); very broad coverage including products, orders, customers, carts, checkout, webhooks, and B2B.
existing_mcp_detail: BigCommerce's official Storefront MCP (launched 2026, natural-language product search/cart/checkout) plus community servers.
notes: BigCommerce is actively pushing agentic-commerce features; authenticated (logged-in) shopping via MCP is noted as coming next.

one_liner: Enterprise cloud commerce platform (B2C/B2B) used by large retail brands for storefronts and order management.
self_serve_evidence: SCAPI/OCAPI access requires an existing, Salesforce-provisioned B2C Commerce org/license plus SLAS or Account Manager credentials — there is no public self-serve signup for the commerce APIs themselves.
api_surface: SCAPI (REST, split into Shopper APIs and Admin APIs) plus legacy OCAPI; broad enterprise commerce coverage (catalog, cart, checkout, orders, customers, pricing, inventory) but scoped to a provisioned instance.
existing_mcp_detail: Community servers exist; no official Commerce-Cloud-specific MCP found (Salesforce's official MCP efforts so far target Agentforce/CRM and Marketing Cloud Engagement).
blocker: Requires an active, provisioned Salesforce B2C Commerce org/license and SLAS/Account Manager setup — no free shared sandbox for a generic third-party integrator.
notes: Enterprise-only platform; existing MCPs are community-built and some focus on developer assistance rather than full transactional coverage.

one_liner: Enterprise e-commerce platform available as self-hosted open source (Magento) or Adobe-managed SaaS (Adobe Commerce Cloud).
self_serve_evidence: Self-hosted Magento Open Source admins can generate integration tokens/OAuth 1.0a keys themselves with no external gate, but Adobe Commerce Cloud (SaaS) requires an Adobe-provisioned subscription/instance.
api_surface: REST API (broad: products, orders, customers, carts, inventory, CMS) plus a GraphQL API for storefront queries.
existing_mcp_detail: Numerous community servers reflecting strong developer demand.
blocker: Requires an existing Magento/Adobe Commerce instance to target — self-hosted setup overhead, or an Adobe Commerce Cloud subscription; no shared multi-tenant developer sandbox.
notes: Unusually large community MCP ecosystem (over a dozen servers found), reflecting strong developer demand despite the setup friction.

one_liner: Website builder and hosting platform with an integrated Commerce offering for online stores.
self_serve_evidence: Merchants on the Commerce Advanced plan can self-serve generate API keys in site settings, but full OAuth2 apps for third-party/commercial distribution require registering through Squarespace's developer program (a gated approval step).
api_surface: REST Commerce APIs covering Products, Orders, Inventory, Transactions, Profiles, Discounts, and Webhooks; only available on the Commerce Advanced plan.
existing_mcp_detail: Community servers exist (e.g. 67-tool Squarespace MCP Server).
blocker: API access is limited to merchants on the Commerce Advanced plan, and full OAuth app distribution requires Squarespace developer registration/approval.
notes: Plan-tier gating (Commerce Advanced only) is the main practical limiter rather than the auth mechanism itself.

one_liner: E-commerce platform (by Lightspeed) that lets merchants embed an online store into any website or social channel.
self_serve_evidence: Developers can register apps and obtain OAuth tokens via Ecwid's documented self-serve flow without a manual approval gate to start building/testing.
api_surface: REST API (JSON) covering store settings, products, categories, orders, customers, discounts, and payment/shipping methods; rate-limited to 600 requests/minute per token.
existing_mcp_detail: An Ecwid connector is listed on the Glama MCP directory.
notes: Smaller MCP community presence than the major platforms, but the core REST API itself is broad and self-serve.

one_liner: Simple e-commerce platform for independent creators to sell digital products, memberships, and subscriptions.
self_serve_evidence: Any Gumroad account holder can create an 'application' from account settings to generate an access token or set up OAuth2, with no approval process required.
api_surface: REST API covering products, sales, subscribers, offer codes, licenses, and resource subscriptions/webhooks — moderate breadth, single-seller focus.
existing_mcp_detail: keithah/gumroad-mcp — MCP server for the Gumroad API covering subscriptions, sales, and products.
notes: The primary help-center article is JS-rendered so full text couldn't be extracted directly; self-serve OAuth/token creation was corroborated via a working community MCP implementation.

one_liner: API suite for Amazon sellers and vendors to manage listings, orders, inventory, pricing, and reports on Amazon's marketplace.
self_serve_evidence: Registration requires submitting a developer profile, a security/data-protection questionnaire, and identity verification, with Amazon reviewing applications against policy and security requirements before granting access.
api_surface: REST APIs, very broad — orders, listings, catalog, inventory, pricing, reports, finances, fulfillment, and notifications — organized as many separate microservice-style API sections.
blocker: Amazon's developer registration/approval process (identity verification, security review, role-based access) gates real API usage, especially for public/third-party apps.
notes: Private apps self-authorized by a seller for their own account are somewhat lighter-weight than public apps, but still require Solution Provider Portal registration and policy compliance.

one_liner: Creator/seller commerce and payments platform (checkout, funnels, subscriptions, affiliates, webinars) that rebranded from FanBasis to Commas in mid-2026.
self_serve_evidence: Commas opened free self-serve account signup at commas.com in 2026 (previously invite-only for sellers), but the developer API docs found sit behind a login wall and a fuller reference could not be fully accessed, so it's unconfirmed whether every account gets an API key or if API access is separately gated/manual.
api_surface: Evidence points to a REST-style API with a /products endpoint, checkout sessions, customers, subscriptions, discount codes, and webhooks, but no complete public reference could be verified end-to-end.
existing_mcp_detail: No dedicated MCP server for FanBasis/Commas was found.
blocker: Could not access complete/authoritative public API documentation — key docs pages are login-gated or JavaScript-rendered SPAs that repeatedly failed to fetch, so self-serve key issuance and full endpoint coverage remain unconfirmed.
notes: This is the deliberately obscure app in the batch. Real API usage was confirmed indirectly via a third-party integration guide, but primary docs could not be reliably fetched/verified, so this is reported honestly as low-confidence rather than guessed.
